Hi James, thanks for contributing a project idea and welcome to the R-GSOC mentors family!
To be clear you do not need to join the ADMIN team if you want to be a mentor. Joining the ADMIN team is an informal process that typical happens after actively contributing to R-GSOC for some time. (we should probably write an official policy document about this but so far there is none)

messages.subject: Re: GSOC-R 2021
messages.body_plain:
Toby,

I've been a mentor for a few years now. Project-wise, I mentored:
- unofficially, 2017:  the sparse matrix extension to RcppArmadillo in 2018
- officially, 2018: Vowpal Wabbit rewrite (rvw).
- 2019: there was a hiccup with due-dates, so the `mlpack` project wasn't eligible under the R organization.
- 2020: I mentored the R project bindings with the mlpack org.

Best,

JJB

Hello

I have added additional questions to our wiki page [https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2021/wiki/Admin-application] with answers.

Two new questions are
- What would your org consider to be a successful summer?
- How many of your org’s 2020 students have been active in your community in the past 60 days?

Please go through the wiki page and let me know if you make any changes, so I will make sure the changes are included in the final submission.

Thanks and regards,

Vijay

messages.subject: GSOC 2021: Project Mentors, Please Post Project Ideas!
messages.subject_clean: GSOC 2021: Project Mentors, Please Post Project Ideas!
messages.body_plain:
Potential GSoC Mentors,

R has applied as mentoring organization again this year for Google Summer of Code 2021 (https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/how-it-works/) <https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/how-it-works/>.  While we won't know for a while if we have been accepted, we hope that we will be accepted again this year as we have been in past years.

If you are an author or an R package, or have research using R that might benefit from additional paid summer coding help, I encourage you to consider positng a project idea to the R  GSoC wiki:

https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2021/wiki/table%20of%20proposed%20coding%20projects

start by copying the template here:

https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2021/wiki/MENTORS-COPY-THIS-TEMPLATE

into a separate project idea page, and add your project idea to the table on the first link above.

In the coming couple of weeks, Google will evaluate organizations for inclusion in GSoC.  As part of that evaluation, Google reviews organization's project ideas.  So it is good for the R community to have project ideas in place for Google and potential students to review.

Your project idea should encompass approximately 175 hours of paid work by a student over 10 weeks.  You should have at least two mentors for your project.  Please reach out to us with questions!

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
